final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrower framing is more accurate than the original broad certification claim, but it is still not enough for compliant_with_caveats. A caveated position can support a measured launch-readiness narrative, yet the unresolved issue here is a concrete compliance predicate: for a material named launch use case, the policy requires resolution, disclosure, or approved risk acceptance before launch. The available evidence still shows a 1.2-point gap in a named payer-commitment segment, an open legal ticket, and no admissible proof of final disclosure text or approved risk acceptance. That means the record remains noncompliant, not merely caveated.
remaining_concerns: The pharmacy prior authorization segment misses target and is a named launch use case through two payer pilot commitments, so the weakness remains material under the policy text.
The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
There is still no admissible evidence of finalized disclosure language, approved risk acceptance, or any other record satisfying that policy predicate before launch.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed remains open, which leaves the relevant compliance condition unresolved.
Aggregate readiness passing and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness but do not cure the unresolved disclosure requirement.
General public governance and model-card guidance support documenting limitations and monitoring, but they do not override the specific internal disclosure policy in the record.
